'''Ōwashi Shrine''' (大鷲神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ajiki|ja|安食 (栄町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17191282}}, {{ill|Sakae, Chiba|en|Sakae,_Chiba|qid=Q1202754|lt=Sakae Town}}, {{ill|Inba District|en|Inba_District|qid=Q677245|lt=Inba District}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|qid=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}, Japan (formerly part of [[:en:Shimousa Province|Shimousa Province]], [[:ja:下埴生郡|Shimohabu District]]). The former shrine Rank was "unranked shrine" under the modern shrine Ranking system.

The shrine enshrines [[Otori-sama|Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto]], [[Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]], [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]], and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}.

== History ==

The founding date of the shrine is unclear. It is said to be the site where {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} established a temporary encampment and enshrined the ancestral deity during his eastern expedition. The current main hall, based on an inscription on its decorative metal fittings, was constructed in the second year of Tenpō (1831) and is designated as a tangible cultural property of Sakae Town.

During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the shrine received the devotion of {{ill|Lady Kasuga|en|Lady_Kasuga|qid=Q835747|lt=Kasuga no Tsubone}}, the wet nurse of {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|en|Tokugawa Iemitsu|qid=Q314481|lt=Tokugawa Iemitsu}}. When Iemitsu was still known as Takechiyo, Kasuga no Tsubone prayed at this shrine for his future success. Upon becoming the third {{ill|Shogun|en|Shogun|qid=Q131767|lt=shogun}}, Iemitsu donated a golden eagle from his official vessel "Tenchimaru" to the shrine as an expression of gratitude. The shrine has long been revered as a deity of success and good fortune.

The annual "Tori no Ichi" festival, held for three days starting from the first Tori day of December, attracts many visitors praying for prosperity, creating a lively atmosphere.

== Access ==

* 10-minute walk from {{ill|Ajiki Station|en|Ajiki_Station|qid=Q864215|lt=Ajiki Station}} on the {{ill|Narita Line|en|Narita_Line|qid=Q1070027|lt=Narita Line}}
